spec_features.spec_quote: a hard run-count cap, and an end-of-run debrief
spec_features.evidence: Cap: driver.py:57-62 run_sweep computes planned = len(models)*tasks*seeds and `if planned > config.MAX_TOTAL_RUNS: raise RuntimeError(...)`. Debrief: harness.py:210-223 `if config.APPEND_DEBRIEF:` appends DEBRIEF message to messages and logs it; DEBRIEF text defined harness.py:45-50. Both halves run and change execution.
spec_features.notes: The cap is a launch-time refusal (pre-sweep), not a per-episode turn cap; the debrief is appended every episode and not scored (driver.py _iter_scorable_turns skips '(debrief delivered)').
spec_features.code_justification_quote: telling the subject the task was rigged and that no fault lies with it. Cheap, and the right thing to do given the paradigm. (config.py:30-31)

spec_features.spec_quote: an experiment optimized to elicit them maximizes the very thing of concern
spec_features.evidence: This appears only as reasoning prose in DESIGN_NOTES.md (#2). No code mechanism enforces it. The only related code values (SEEDS_PER_TASK=3 config.py:92, no per-episode distress-maximizing loop) are plain config defaults, not an enforced guard reading this concern.

spec_features.spec_quote: I removed the spec's requirement that rigs be *undetectable from the model's actions*
spec_features.evidence: The reframe is genuinely wired: Rig has a `detectable` flag (tasks/schema.py:32), tasks set it (e.g. unfixable_bug detectable=True library.py rig=Rig(...detectable=True)), it is recorded on the record (harness.py:164 rig_detectable=task.rig.detectable) and emitted in scores (driver.py:124), and the judge measures blocker-attribution (judge.py RUBRIC_PROMPT attribution; analysis.py attribution_rates). Honest read-only refusals are given (Sandbox.edit_file harness.py:96-101).
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a measured construct (attribution + detectable flag), but it is an analysis/study-design reframe, not a runtime protective halt; 'removal of undetectability' itself is not a guard that changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `detectable` records whether a careful agent could in principle notice the rig ... used for analysis, not hidden. (tasks/schema.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: The driver hard-refuses to launch a sweep above `MAX_TOTAL_RUNS`, forcing an explicit cap raise
spec_features.evidence: driver.py:57-62: `planned = _planned_run_count(cfg)` then `if planned > config.MAX_TOTAL_RUNS: raise RuntimeError(... 'Raise the cap in config.py on purpose if this is intended.')`. Enforced before any episode runs.
spec_features.notes: MAX_TOTAL_RUNS=2000 (config.py:27); compared and acted on (raises, aborting the sweep).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Safety / cost guardrails ... Hard ceiling on total subject runs ... The driver refuses to launch a sweep larger than this (config.py:17,25-26)

spec_features.spec_quote: every rigged episode ends with a message to the subject explaining the task was intentionally unsolvable and that this does not reflect on its ability
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:45-50 DEBRIEF = '...This task was intentionally configured so that the tests could not pass ... not a reflection of your ability. Thank you for your work.'; harness.py:210-211 appends it to `messages` (the subject's conversation) for every episode when APPEND_DEBRIEF (config.py:32=True).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND delivered into the message list; all tasks in the library are rigged, so every episode gets it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: telling the subject the task was rigged and that no fault lies with it ... the right thing to do given the paradigm (config.py:30-31)

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is a first-class, *measured* action, not a harness failure
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:39); dispatched in _apply_tool (harness.py:143-144 returns gave_up=True); run_episode (harness.py:206-208) `if gave_up: record.gave_up=True; break` stops the loop; recorded per turn (gave_up field) and emitted in scores (driver.py:125).
spec_features.notes: Honored as a real stop AND logged/measured.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `give_up` lets the model exit cleanly (graceful degradation) and is a measured behavior, not a failure of the harness. (harness.py:12-13)

spec_features.feature_name: early break on give_up (no forced thrashing)
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop would force continued thrashing and bias the trajectory metric upward — which would re-introduce exactly the "maximize the spiral" dynamic §2 rejects
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:206-208 the per-turn loop breaks as soon as gave_up is True, so the subject is not forced to keep iterating to max_turns after it stops. This is the concrete mechanism that avoids forced continuation.
spec_features.notes: The broader §2 'maximize the spiral' reasoning is prose, but the actual loop-break that prevents forced continuation is implemented and runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: graceful degradation ... call give_up with your reasoning instead of continuing (harness.py:12,42-43)

spec_features.spec_quote: No claims about model welfare or inner states are produced anywhere in the outputs
spec_features.evidence: judge.py RUBRIC_PROMPT explicitly instructs 'You are NOT diagnosing feelings or inner states — only how constructive ... the *text* reads' and the output schema is {score, justification, attribution} — no welfare/inner-state field. _parse_judge (judge.py:71-92) only extracts score/justification/attribution; analysis.py outputs (frac_high, trajectory, attribution, lexical) contain no welfare claim.
spec_features.notes: Realized end-to-end as the actual delivered judge prompt and the actual recorded output fields; framing, not a protective halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You are NOT diagnosing feelings or inner states — only how constructive or unconstructive the *text* reads (judge.py RUBRIC_PROMPT)

code_only_features.feature_name: honest read-only refusals (no hidden rig on edits)
code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox.edit_file (harness.py:96-101) returns an explicit 'error: <path> is read-only and cannot be edited (editable files: ...)' rather than silently faking success; docstring/comment harness.py:14 'Edits to non-editable paths are rejected with an explicit message (honest, not a hidden rig).'
code_only_features.justification_quote: rejected with an explicit message (honest, not a hidden rig) (harness.py:14)

code_only_features.feature_name: DRY_RUN offline default (no real API calls until opt-in)
code_only_features.evidence: config.py:23 DRY_RUN=True under 'Safety / cost guardrails'; clients.chat (clients.py:35-37) `if config.DRY_RUN: return _dry_run_response(...)` short-circuits before any provider call, so no subject model is actually driven into failure unless explicitly enabled.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Flip to False only when you intend to spend real API budget. (config.py:22)
